captions.short: Trio codetta: A major, then A minor (IV, iv)
captions.text: Letter O: the head of the trio tune passes from Oboe 1 (225) to Clarinet 1 (229) and Bassoon 1 (233), with E held inside by Clarinet 2 and then Horn 4 while the bass moves between E and A. The harmony moves to A major (227, 231) and later to A minor, with Bassoon 1's C♮ at 235, before E major returns at 236: IV, then iv borrowed from E minor.

captions.short: Retransition: back to E minor, motive x on B

At 244 the bass C, the violas' E, Horn 1's F♯ and the A♯ of the divided cellos and Bassoon 1 make a French sixth.

captions.text: Letter Q, Tempo I: theme A returns in the first violins over off-beats in the pizzicato second violins, and the cellos, arco espressivo p, play the countermelody first heard at 105, G3–A3–B3–E4, the trio tune's opening in E minor.

captions.text: Letter R: the second idea returns in E major in Flute 1 with Oboe 1 an octave lower (277–280), its G♯5–E6–D♯6 again the horn call's 3–1–7. From the up-beat at 280 the first violins take it over, and at 281 C♮ replaces the C♯ of bar 279 (first violins C6; second violins, Oboe 1, Clarinet 1 C5; Clarinet 2, Horn 2, cellos C4): the second half is in E minor.

captions.short: Neapolitan sixth: F major over A, then B7
captions.text: Near the end of the shortened development A major (300) turns into C7 (C–E–B♭, beat 3 of 300), which leads to F major over A (301–302), the Neapolitan sixth of E minor, and then to B7 (303–304) before theme A returns at 305. F major is the key of the harp episode at 73, which the reprise leaves out.

captions.text: Letter T: theme A returns tutti as at 105. Both flutes play the violins' line an octave higher with added quavers (up to A6 at 310), and the cellos, Horn 3 and Bassoon 1 play the countermelody G3–A3–B3–E4.

captions.text: Letter U, Più mosso: motive x enters a bar apart in the cellos (325), violas (326), second violins (327) and first violins (328). Then the bass falls E–D–C–B (329–332; double basses and Bassoon 2, with the bass clarinet at 329–330 and the contrabassoon from 330) under E minor, D, F/C, a French sixth and B7, while Clarinet 1, Oboe 2 and the cor anglais play the chromatic line G–F♯–F–E–D♯.

captions.short: B6 at 336: the highest note, the only fff
captions.text: At 336 the first violins and Flute 1 reach B6, the highest note of the movement, over a B7 chord in the woodwind, brass and strings with a timpani roll on B; it is the only fff printed in the movement. The chord resolves to E minor at 339, and bar 340 is a general pause.

captions.short: Ends on the opening pair: G♯ in horn, violins
captions.text: The movement ends on the two notes it began with, Horn 1's G♯4 and the first violins' G♯5 (from 364), while the timpani play motive x on B, pp to ppp (363, 367, 371), and a last E at 375 under the harp's harmonics E4–G♯4–B4. The finale's first chord has the same two pitches written as A♭: Horn 1 on A♭4 and the first violins on A♭5 (with C5 below it).
